newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to seek French support for NATO, EU entry.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to seek French support for NATO, EU entry.

text.p: Bulgaria's reformist President Petar Stoyanov left for Paris on Thursday hoping to encourage French investment in his country and boost its chances of entering the European Union and NATO.

"The main areas of discussion will be Bulgaria's successful, albeit delayed, launch of market reforms and our clear will to integrate with the EU and NATO...and the support we could expect from Europe, and France in particular," Stoyanov told reporters on departure from Sofia airport.
Stoyanov is expected to meet President Jacques Chirac and Prime Minister Alain Juppe during his three-day visit to France, said the president's spokeswoman.
"I hope to convince our French counterparts that our reforms are aimed at forming an attractive business climate for foreign investors," said Stoyanov.
He is accompanied by Industry Minister Alexander Bozhkov and a group of businessmen.

Bulgaria has an association agreement with the EU, but delayed reforms and economic mismanagement caused an unprecedented financial crisis earlier this year, which led to early elections on April 19 won by the United Democratic Front.
Last month Bulgaria reached a $657 million reform and funding deal with the International Monetary Fund to help it on the path to economic recovery.

Bulgaria is among several countries lobbying for inclusion in NATO's first eastward expansion to be announced at a summit in Madrid in July. But Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are seen as more certain candidates.
